The onset of gonadal activity at this length corresponds to a wet weight at puberty of about 365 grams [Wwp = about 365 grams], a value derived from length-weight regressions fitted to a large sample of specimens captured across the seasonal upwelling regime of the Gulf of Guinea. This pattern of delayed maturity relative to maximum size is consistent with an iteroparous life-history strategy that prioritises somatic growth before channelling resources toward reproduction. Comparative data from related sciaenids suggest that the length at which 50 percent of individuals are mature may vary slightly with local exploitation pressure, but the figure of 35 centimeters remains a reliable benchmark for unimpacted populations.
